input.prompt:
In this Next.js + Mantine repo (footy league app), I'm investigating a failing test at src/app/footy/auth/claim/[token]/page.vitest.spec.tsx:73 which expects the rendered error state to contain `href="/footy"` (i.e., a link back to the home/footy page) when an invitation link is invalid. The current page component at src/app/footy/auth/claim/[token]/page.tsx does NOT render any such link — it only renders a Mantine <Notification> with the error message, no <Anchor>.

I need to know: is there an existing convention elsewhere in this codebase for other "invalid token/link" pages (e.g. password reset, email verification, other claim/invite flows) that render a link back to "/footy" alongside an error notification? Look for other page.tsx files under src/app/footy/auth/** or similar error-state pages, and check how they render error notifications and whether they include an Anchor/Link back to "/footy" or home.

Report back: 
1. Whether such a convention exists (with file:line references)
2. What the exact JSX pattern looks like (e.g., Anchor href="/footy" text, placement relative to Notification)
so I can decide whether to fix the page component (add the missing link) or fix the test (remove the incorrect expectation).

content.text: I've kicked off a search to see whether other error-state auth pages in this repo already follow a "link back to /footy" convention.
